thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High GPU queue growth detected in us-west-2 pool 'prod-gpu-a' — autoscaler failing to provision, error rate rising, paging on-call.
Eva L: I'm on it, grabbing on-call. what's the customer impact?
Jorge S: Tickets from two customers showing 503s for generation endpoints, a handful of timeouts from batches. not widespread yet but steady.
Sam K: Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up attempts that time out during driver init on new nodes: driver init failing with CUDA Xid 45 and OOM reports.
Neal R: Xid 45 usually points to kernel driver faults during warmup. could be a bad driver rollout or kernel mismatch. any recent driver pushes?
Maria P: I see a driver rollout yesterday to the canary fleet, but rollout was paused. however, a subset of nodes were manually patched. threading that to infra now.
Eva L: @Sam K can you post the autoscaler error snippet?
Sam K: sure — logs:
```
autoscaler: scale_attempt=3 node_request_id=abc123 status=timeout
node-init: fetch-driver=ok unpack=ok modprobe=ok run-driver-service=failed
runtime: nvml_error=74 cuda_xid=45 kernel-oom=true
```
Neal R: That runtime line is consistent with a kernel-level panic while initializing NV driver. nodes then drop from pool and cause queue to pile up.
Jorge S: Customer impact: latency spikes from 300ms -> 3-10s and some 503s. Support flagged two high-visibility customers.
Eva L: Triage plan: 1) Quarantine flagged new nodes from pool 2) Force autoscaler to prefer older driver AMIs in us-west-2 3) Hot-replace saturated requests to dedicated backup pool (if available) 4) Page infra to rollback canary.
Sam K: Running quarantine now — marking nodes with tag 'quarantine-driver-4991234567'. also bumping autoscale timeout to allow init to finish but that's risky.
deploy-bot: deploy: rollback request queued for driver-canary -> version v1.2.3 -> rollback to v1.2.2 by @Sam K
Neal R: If rollback won't finish quick enough, we should route new requests to a different region (us-east-1) with healthy capacity. That will reduce latency for some customers but keeps service up.
Maria P: I'm opening a routing policy change in the console — creating a temporary region-fallback policy for the affected routes. ETA ~6m.
Jorge S: Notifying affected customers: prepared a short blurb — ETA 10m to confirm mitigation.
Eva L: On-call handoff: @Sam K you're primary for infra, @Neal R you're runtime lead, @Maria P handle routing & customer comms; I'll coordinate postmortem.
Sam K: Quarantine complete, 8 nodes flagged, preventing new allocations. Autoscaler now preferring older AMI.
Neal R: Checking kube logs on flagged nodes — found repeated OOM during driver module load:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 45, PID 2048, Thread 7
[ 1234.567891] Out of memory in module init
```
Neal R: Looks like a kernel/driver binary mismatch causing alloc path to blow up.
Maria P: Region-fallback policy applied. Traffic split 70% us-west-2 -> us-east-1. Latency for impacted customers dropped back to ~500ms. 503s reduced.
Jorge S: Customer comms sent to the two high-visibility accounts, support prepping follow-up.
Sam K: Kicking off rollback to v1.2.2 now. nodes will be re-imaged; ETA 15m.
incident-bot: Pager acknowledged by Eva L, incident status: mitigation-in-progress.
Neal R: While rollback proceeds, we should add a temporary safety check to autoscaler to avoid draining below healthy thresholds; I'll open PR to patch the scale policy. small patch, can ship in a few mins.
Eva L: Good. Also create a prompt to reroute long-running batches to a CPU-fallback path if GPU queuing persists — reduce failed requests.
Sam K: Rollback completed on 6/8 nodes so far. Two nodes still cycling due to missing artifacts — investigating.
Maria P: Observability: queue depth peaked at 1.2k requests, now decaying to ~200. error rate trending down. I'll keep dashboards in pinned.
Jorge S: Support says impacted customers acknowledged the temporary routing and appreciate the quick update.
Neal R: After full rollback we should quarantine the images used for the canary and run extra integration to catch this mismatch in future.
Eva L: Agreed. Postmortem owners: Neal R (runtime root cause), Sam K (infra/rollback), Maria P (customer impact & routing), me (timeline & mitigations).
Sam K: Leaving a note: we need better preflight for driver AMIs and a canary gating test for kernel mod init.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Handing off to follow-up channel for postmortem.
Eva L: Thanks all — handing this to postmortems channel, will ping when draft is ready. :white_check_mark:
